conventions.frame: X = body axis, flow +X (nose at x = 0), Z up, right-handed
conventions.radius: radius_mm is perpendicular to the body axis (not along the coned span)
conventions.rotation: right-handed about +X (Omega vector +X): CLOCKWISE seen from upstream (observer at the nose looking downstream). A blade pointing +Z moves toward -Y.
conventions.twist: angle between chord line and the plane of rotation, measured in the section plane normal to the pitch axis; POSITIVE = leading edge rotated upstream (-X). Angle of attack = inflow angle phi - twist.
conventions.section_orientation: suction (convex, upper) side faces downstream (+X); leading edge points in the direction of rotation
conventions.section_placement: for the blade whose axis is in the +Z half-plane: pitch-axis point A = (pitch_axis_x_mm, 0, radius_mm); e_n = (cos b, 0, -sin b) with b = cone; d = cos(tw) * (+Y) + sin(tw) * e_n (LE -> TE); n = cos(tw) * e_n - sin(tw) * (+Y) (toward suction side). Section point = A + chord * ((xs - pitch_axis) * d + ys * n) for unit-chord coordinates (xs, ys) of hydroegg.bem.naca44_section.
conventions.cone: aft (+X) lean of the pitch axis out of the plane of rotation, about the tangential hinge pin

rotor.cone_note: straight pitch axis at the nominal cone; the hull-following curved axis is evaluated as a sensitivity (see sensitivity)

section.family: NACA 44xx (4 % camber at 40 % chord), t/c linear root to tip
section.te_construction: closed-TE NACA thickness (-0.1036 x^4) plus a linear add-on 0.5 * te * (x/c) on each surface normal to the chord (CST TE term)
section.naca_code_note: codes are rounded labels; use thickness_ratio for geometry

stations.hinge_dependent_note: pitch_axis_x_mm, pitch_axis_aft_of_hinge_mm and span_from_hinge_mm are provisional (params.py hinge, straight axis); see provisional

pitch_axis_hull_following_estimate.note: estimate only, for the layout study: pitch axis that would copy the hull when folded 90 deg forward about the hinge; Cp change vs the straight 12 deg axis is in sensitivity

shank.blend: loft from the lug at the hinge to the NACA root section at r_end_mm; aerodynamically inactive (BEM span starts at r_aero_root_mm, hub loss there)
shank.status: provisional: hinge from params.py, see provisional

performance.note: MPPT = generator load held at the Cp-peak TSR; fixed = load held at the design TSR; runaway = zero torque (free-wheeling); flap/edge moments per blade about the hinge pin, flap positive pushes the blade aft onto its deployed stop. The hinge moments are provisional (params.py hinge, see provisional and layout_axis_check)

tsr_study_note: cp_constrained = Cp of the printable linear blade optimised for that TSR, flown at that TSR; tsr_constrained_peak = where its Cp actually peaks. copper_loss_index = (torque / torque of the chosen design)^2 at 1.5 m/s, same generator (copper loss scales with current squared, current with torque)
generator_tradeoff_note: final blade at 1.5 m/s held at TSR at or above its Cp peak: copper_loss_index = (torque / torque at the Cp peak)^2

generator_coupling_estimate.model: ESTIMATE: torque_e = torque - drag; I = torque_e / Kt0, Kt0 = 60 / (2 pi KV); copper loss I^2 R_ll; net = torque_e omega - copper loss at the AC terminals; rectifier and cable losses excluded
generator_coupling_estimate.runaway_emf_note: open-circuit (free-wheeling) line-line peak EMF = rpm / KV

load_line_by_flow.note: ESTIMATE. Final blade on the 0.1 m/s flow grid. unconstrained = best net power on the 0.25 TSR grid; capped = best point with cavitation margin >= cav_margin_cap (grid points plus the exact cap point, tip at depth_m); rpm_ceiling = best such point at or below rpm_ceiling_fixed; *_cost_pct = net power lost against unconstrained (a capped point slightly above the grid optimum counts as 0). tsr_cavitation_free_to (margin 0) is interpolated on the sweep, tsr_cap is solved; null = no limit below the end of the TSR sweep.
load_line_by_flow.cav_margin_cap_reason: an inviscid Hess-Smith panel check of the tip sections gives margins 0.02 to 0.04 lower than the NeuralFoil Cp_min near the limits
load_line_by_flow.rpm_ceiling_fixed_note: lowest cap rpm among the flows where the cap lies below runaway TSR: a single rpm limit that keeps the cap margin at every flow up to the end of the grid

cap_torque_curve.rule: cavitation-free (margin >= cav_margin_cap) if rpm < rpm[0], or rpm <= rpm[-1] and shaft torque >= min_shaft_torque_Nm interpolated in rpm; above rpm[-1] not studied
cap_torque_curve.check_scope: every final-blade sweep point on the 0.1 m/s flow grid from the Cp peak to runaway (positive torque)

tsr_rule: highest candidate TSR whose constrained Cp is within 0.5 % of the best

constraint_chain.label: + linear chord and twist (best linear law, no bounds)
+ 12 deg aft cone = final blade (re-optimised, rounded)
0.7R-0.9R line through it (optimiser start, not optimised)

structure_estimates.assumptions: solid PLA 1240 kg/m^3, straight pitch axis at the nominal cone, hinge moments applied to the 22 x 8 mm stadium lug (upper bound)
structure_estimates.status: provisional: hinge from params.py, see provisional

cavitation_vs_tsr.note: final blade, tip at the top of its circle at depth_m; margin = sigma + Cp_min (worst element); tsr_free_from/to = TSR window around the Cp peak with margin >= 0

root_elements.note: elements 0 and 1 (the only ones that ever fail to converge): width and share of the rotor torque, final blade

convergence_audit.scope: every solve whose numbers reach this file or the figures, except the sensitivity cases (separate Study objects); unconverged elements keep their last iterate

constraint_chain_note: cumulative steps in order optimum, te, linear, chord, twist, final; every linear-law step is re-optimised (multi-start Nelder-Mead) under all constraints so far, so a step's cost is its constraint's own; iso_* = one constraint applied alone to the blunt-TE optimum; fit_0p7_0p9 = straight lines through the blunt-TE optimum at 0.7R and 0.9R (optimiser start, not optimised); schmitz = reference

constraint_chain_check.note: x = (chord root mm, chord tip mm, twist root deg, twist tip deg); the final step re-optimised with the chain's tight multi-start vs the final blade x_final (single start, rounded to 0.1 mm / 0.1 deg)

layout_axis_check.source: data/layout_rotor.json: chosen.hinge_x_mm, chosen.hinge_r_mm, axis (r_mm, aft_mm, cone_local_deg)
layout_axis_check.note: final blade (same chord, twist, sections) flown on the layout study's curved pitch axis and hinge; flap/edge moments per blade about that hinge; in-plane lead of the axis ignored. The nominal-axis columns repeat this file's params.py-hinge values.

provisional.status: PROVISIONAL: computed with the params.py hinge (x 116 mm, r 14 mm) and a straight 12 deg pitch axis, as the BEM brief specified. The rotor layout study (data/layout_rotor.json) moved the hinge to (x 116, r 14) mm with a curved axis; layout_axis_check gives the loads on that geometry. Do not size the hinge, stop or lug from these fields; re-run this study once the layout hinge and axis are promoted to params.py.
provisional.not_affected: chord, twist, sections, Cp, power, torque, thrust and rpm do not depend on the hinge position (layout_axis_check compares the Cp peak on both axes)
